name: Let's Play Facecam
summary: Game footage fills the frame and a small live window of the player's face sits in one corner. The face reacts, and loud captions and zoom cuts push the mood.

philosophy.core_thesis: The game is the stage and the face is the audience: put the reaction next to the action, and the viewer follows the player, not the game.
design_principles: Fill the frame with game footage and set the facecam window at 18% to 25% of the frame width.
Place the facecam in a corner at 24px from each edge and keep it there for the full clip.
Crop the facecam to a rounded box with a 4px border in the accent colour.
Zoom the face by 110% to 130% for 8 to 12 frames at a scare or a win, then return.
Add a red or yellow caption of 48px to 72px with a 4px black outline for the key joke.
Cut every pause over 1.5s and add a short sound hit at each cut.
Keep the game HUD visible; do not cover the health bar or the map with the facecam.
anti_patterns: Studio lighting that removes the room
A facecam that covers the game HUD
Silent, still footage with no cuts
Small, thin captions that fade into the game
A corporate lower-third with a logo bar

layout.grid_mechanics: A 16:9 frame with two layers: full-bleed game footage and a facecam box of 18% to 25% width at a corner, on a 24px safe margin.
layout.whitespace_ratio: Under 5% of the frame is empty; the game and the face use all of it.
layout.alignment_rules: The facecam sits at a corner, usually bottom-left or bottom-right; captions centre on the lower third.
layout.container_geometry: A facecam box with a 12px radius and a 4px accent border; captions use a 4px outline instead of a box.

font_pairings.note: Anton is an open look-alike of the Impact face that gamers use for captions.
A comic caption face for jokes and sound words.
A thick, round display face for big reactions.

hierarchy_rules: Use one display weight (400) and a body weight of 500.
Set the main caption in capitals at 56px to 72px with a 4px outline.
Set the channel name at 24px in the accent colour.

color.palette_structure: A game-neutral dark frame with hot red and warm yellow for captions, and one cyan border for the facecam.
color.contrast_rules: White text on screen black holds at least 17:1; captions also carry a 4px black outline so that they read on any game scene.
color.surface_treatment: Flat dark panels; the game footage is the only texture.
color.light_and_shadow: No cast shadow; a 4px black outline separates text from the picture, and the facecam keeps a 3px accent glow.

materiality.surface_simulation: A monitor capture: sharp game pixels and a webcam image with room light and slight compression noise.
materiality.border_rules: A 4px border in cyan on the facecam; a 4px black outline on caption text.
materiality.blur_and_elevation: No blur; the facecam sits flat above the game with a 4px hard shadow.

ornamentation_details.iconography: Solid icons at 24px for sound, subscribe and like; square terminals and a thick 3px edge.
ornamentation_details.illustration: Game footage, a webcam face, arrows and circles in red; sticker faces at 64px for jokes.

motion.transition_physics: The facecam punches in by 20% over 120ms at a peak moment; captions pop in at 110% size and settle to 100% over 160ms; each cut lands on a sound hit.
motion.hover_and_active: Hover lifts a button by 2px with a 4px hard shadow; active state flips the fill to yellow.

emotion.target_response: The viewer feels part of a shared, loud and funny moment with the player.

use_cases: game launch trailers with a host
avoid_when: The audience expects a calm, adult tone.
The product is not a game or an app demo.
The face of a person cannot appear.

modifiers.how: Add a full frame with a name bar, alert boxes and a chat panel; keep the facecam.
Replace the shouted captions with a steady voice, clean subtitles and a 12% black vignette.
Freeze the funniest facecam frame, enlarge the face to 60% of the frame and add a 120px headline.

pack.why: A thick, solid family matches the loud, high-contrast captions and the bold game frame.

ground.why: The ground is a dark monitor image with fine scanlines, the screen that the game runs on.
